correctness.rationale: I reconstructed the full random-merger-history count: independently uniformly ordering the k coalescent blocks yields a uniform composition of n into k positive parts, with conditional independent uniform within-block merger histories. The displayed factorial moments for singleton B and doubleton D follow by selecting specified part sizes; regression E[C|partition]=(n−B+D)/3+B(B−1)/[3(k−1)] includes cherries already formed and future singleton merges. Multiplication by D and moments give the stated covariance, with k=n−1 and n deterministic boundaries. Holding times are independent of the merger chain with mean 2/[k(k−1)], and the polynomial sum gives 5/18 exactly. As an independent finite corroboration, re-enumerated all 59,602 labeled merger histories n=2..7 and obtained the full small-sample covariance and intermediate level values, plus E L_n2=1; the all-n proof is algebraic, not extrapolated. Mutation consequence follows by conditional Poisson expectation.
residual_risks: Only pairwise unit-rate binary Kingman coalescent; mutation corollary requires independent Poisson infinite-sites process.
Conditional composition derivation is critical; finite n enumeration does not certify all sample sizes.

checked_sources: Same Kingman genealogy model in Disanto–Wiehe and Birkner–Blath–Eldon
Exact n-uniform covariance formula and its proof
value.rationale: The surprising nonzero positive topology–branch-length association, constant at 5/18 for every n≥5 despite E[C_n] growing linearly, is a natural exact genealogical mixed moment. The levelwise positive formula and immediate site-frequency mutation covariance can be reused in uncertainty quantification and joint coalescent statistics. It is not a minor marginal-count restatement.
residual_risks: Result does not give a full joint distribution, different merger rates, or demographic variation.

final_claim: For all n≥5 and 2≤k≤n in unit-pair-rate binary Kingman coalescent, Cov(C_n,D_nk)=k(k−1)(n−k)(n−k−1)(n+k−6)/[3(n−1)(n−2)(n−3)(n−4)], giving strictly positive intermediate levels and Cov(C_n,L_n2)=5/18; n=4 gives 4/9, n=2,3 zero; E[L_n2]=1 for n≥3.
limitations: Exact binary Kingman unit pair rates; fixed-n moment only, no full joint law or multiple mergers.
